subject.title: Renderer placeholder leak: `(see attached image)`, `Image reply`, `Audio reply`, `Media reply` leak to human-visible Telegram reply under specific content-classification paths

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor an instrumented Telegram reproduction now, or require the reporter to supply a redacted outbound-boundary trace before implementation begins?
rationale: The claimed user-visible corruption is serious enough to investigate, but the current evidence spans separate prompt, transcript, and channel surfaces without identifying the crossing point, so choosing who supplies the missing live proof requires maintainer ownership.

options.title: Require Boundary Trace
options.body: Ask for a redacted trace of the normalized reply, transcript text, media blocks, final Telegram send payload, and observed chat result before assigning code work.

options.title: Sponsor Live Telegram Reproduction
options.body: Have a Telegram-area owner run the reported reply-directive and media-only scenarios with temporary boundary instrumentation against current main.

recommendation.title: Require Boundary Trace
recommendation.body: Ask for a redacted trace of the normalized reply, transcript text, media blocks, final Telegram send payload, and observed chat result before assigning code work.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Telegram rich-delivery history and explicit routing into this issue make this person the best available owner for deciding the channel-proof path.
